findings.title: Cutover can report success when verification exits nonzero
findings.description: `_repair` logs a nonzero subprocess return code but returns only the captured text. The acceptance checks in `main` decide success by searching for `FAIL` and `[WAIT]`, without checking that return code. For example, `--verify` can exit 2 with `scan refused: ...` and no such marker, causing the cutover to report `CUTOVER COMPLETE` despite having no verification result. Propagate the status and fail acceptance on any unsuccessful verification.

findings.title: Minute firing is not stopped when the trailing phase completes
findings.description: `fire_unit_until` calls `run(["mt-run", ...], stream=True)` before polling for the journal marker. `run` uses blocking `subprocess.run`, and the inspected `deploy/mt-run` waits for the systemd unit to finish before returning. Consequently, the marker is checked only after the minute unit has ended; the cutover cannot stop it at trailing-phase completion and may wait through the unbounded backfill it was intended to avoid. Start the firing without blocking the marker poll.

findings.title: Sudoers permits root execution of operator-writable code
findings.description: `MT_INSTALL` grants root execution of `install-production.sh` from the operator’s checkout. Since the operator can modify that checkout, this grants the `manta` account a path to run arbitrary code as root. `MT_RUN` also allows arbitrary arguments to the root wrapper, whose non-wrapper commands are passed through to the production CLI. Restrict privileged commands to root-owned, non-writable executables and narrowly defined arguments.

findings.title: Freshness probe does not normalize an uninitialized refresh timestamp
findings.description: The query returns `stats.last_successful_finish` directly. The existing `cagg_freshness` implementation documents that TimescaleDB can report `-infinity` before a policy has completed and that psycopg raises while decoding it; that implementation normalizes the value with `NULLIF`. Here, a never-successful refresh can instead abort `--verify` with a database decoding error rather than return a stale/WAIT verdict. Normalize this timestamp before fetching it.
